decisions.decision: The work will store deadlines as optional fields in the existing version 1 ticket file and rely on operators to retain the upgraded data for reactivation because 1.4.0 can read the file but drops deadlines when it saves.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected original deadlines to survive normal 1.4.0 writes and a later re-upgrade without operators having to retain deadline data separately.

decisions.decision: An invalid response-hours override will stop startup and the error will name the setting.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the service to start with the default hours for that priority and warn the operator about the invalid override.

decisions.decision: For a legacy ticket whose priority was edited before rollout, the backfill will use the priority in the saved ticket record.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have intended to use the priority at creation, recovered from the ticket's audit history.

decisions.decision: When an overdue query includes both status and priority, a ticket must be overdue and match either of those two filters, preserving the service's existing OR behavior.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected overdue tickets to match both supplied filters, as the existing API documentation describes for status and priority.

decisions.decision: The work will deliver the source locally and leave production activation to the operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected delivery to include preparing the production service configuration and carrying out the staged activation.
decisions.where: record/04-spec.md:50 (summary) and repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md:7 and :25 (Targets and runtimes, Access and accounts)

decisions.decision: The startup backfill will assign deadlines without adding entries to ticket audit histories.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected each backfilled ticket's history to record when its deadline was assigned.

decisions.decision: The overdue filter will run before cursor pagination, so the cursor and page size apply to matching tickets.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted the filter to narrow each existing ticket page while keeping the unfiltered page boundaries.

decisions.decision: The HTTP API will return due as an ISO 8601 timestamp string in UTC.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected the API to return a numeric Unix timestamp.
